newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 16.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Former Rugby Union Kangaroo winger Willie Carne broke his jaw in the return interstate rugby match with New South Wales on Saturday night after mistiming a tackle at the Sydney Footbal Stadium in a match won 33-9 by the Waratahs. Carne is scheduled for surgery this morning. Page 27

Australian Football League team Port Adelaide overcame a 40-point quarter-time deficit to defeat League leaders Western Bulldogs 82-94 in an Australian Football League match at the Optus Oval on Saturday. The win gives Port a very real chance to make the final eight in their first season. Page 28

Despite tipping sideways at Rosehill on Saturday, Jockey Shane Dye has vowed not to alter his 'short' riding style which is taking him towards his second Sydney jockeys' title. While Dye says the shorter style gives him greater balance and control, othrs argue that the practice increases the element of danger. Page 29
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Rugby League officials have defended themselves against allegations the League is going soft on drug taking amid claims the Australian Sports Drug Agency is disappointed with ARL's action on recent drug positives.Page 27

London Super League coach Tony Currie has called for the World Cup Challenge to be scaled down after his team was defeated 66-20 by the Canberra Raiders at Bruce Stadium yesterday. Currie said he was embrrassed by some of his players' defence and even hinted he would be sacking some from the club. Page 27

Sydney Kings basketball coach Alan Black has rated his team outstanding after reaching the top-four in the Australian National Basketball League. The Kings managed two away victories over the weekend with a 106-96 win over the Melbourne Tigers, and a 114-99 win over the Adelaide 36ers. Page 30
THE AGE

The Melbourne Tigers basketball team has axed American import Jarvis Lang due to his degenerative knee condition, discovered during a recent operation. Lang's chronic knee problems had restricted him to 19 points and nine rebounds in five games. He was sidelined for six weeks and made a two game comeback before his knee problems flared again. Page 17

Ford touring car driver Glenn Seton lost a commanding lead in the national touring car series at Lakeside near Brisbane yesterday when he crashed out of the seventh round. Seton posted a lap record of 52.4 seconds and was leading the second race when his braking mistake occurred in the uphill Eastern Loop section of the track. Page 18

Top Australian triathlete Emma Carney easily won the national duathlon championships at Kew Boulevard yesterday despite an inclement Melbourne morning. A winter equavalent of the triathlon, the duathlon consisted by a 10 kilometre run, 40 kilometre cycle and a five kilometre run. Page 20
THE HERALD SUN

Australia's Young Socceroos coach Les Scheinflug is confident of success in today's World Youth Soccer Championships in Malaysia despite losing two key players, Kasey Wehrman and Simon Colosimo, from his 18-man squad. The Aussies are in Group E, based in Kangar. Page 79.

Melbourne Knights soccer players Damian Vojtek and Ante Deak have rejected a $10,000 a month offer to play at China's Matsunichi club after both became homesick two days after joining. The young pair returned to continue their loan stint with North Geelong yesterday. Page 79.

Defending champions Adelaide Lightning defeated the Perth Breakers 76-57 to retain second placing in the Australian women's national basketball league yesterday. Adelaide captain Rachael Sporn scored 24 points and 13 rebounds Page 79.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian cyclists Robbie McEwen and Jay Sweet took top positions in two overseas competitions over the weekend. Queenslander McEwen won the 134 kilometre road leg of the Tour of Luxembourg, while South Australian Sweet was declared winner in a stage of the Tour of America.

AFL Swan's captain Paul Kelly received a left shoulder injury on Friday night's clash against Richmond, leaving him out of next weekend's State of Origin series and possibly Sydney's grand final replay the week after. Page 34.

A $1.5 million package has been offered by the Australian and Queensland rugby unions to retain Reds pair Ben Tune and Elton Flately. Tune is expected to sign a three year contract worth about $900,000, while Flatley is being offered $600,000 for the same period. Page 45.
